passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Chapter law text shows HB2853 made ESA eligibility universal; the chapter's unchanged "qualified school" definition in the same snapshot covers nongovernmental (including religious) schools.
Bill overview lists Wilmeth as a co-sponsor of HB2853, the single-subject ESA expansion bill signed by the governor.
House Third Reading vote detail shows Wilmeth voted Y on HB2853's final passage, 31-26-3-0-0, a contested rather than near-unanimous vote.

rows.reasoning: Wilmeth co-sponsored and voted Y on HB2853 (2022), which amended Arizona's empowerment scholarship account law so that "qualified student" includes any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" who does not otherwise already qualify, making ESA eligibility universal rather than limited to most families. This matches the rung text "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family," and the bill passed the House 31-26, a contested single-subject vote, not near-unanimous.
